text:
Kai: Quick follow-up to the onboard rotation convo. I want to propose a preservation + canary pool strategy instead of full random rotation. Key goals: keep a stable regression baseline, introduce fresh coverage, and have a tiny canary set that runs on every rollout. Thoughts?

Maria: Sounds good. Can you sketch the pools?

Kai: Sure:
- preserved_baseline: 5-10% of goldset, frozen for 90d, used for long-term regression detection.
- rolling_pool: ~15% updated weekly (stratified).
- canary_pool: tiny (20 samples) that run on every canary/dry-run and must pass before traffic shifts.

Sanjay: I like separating preserved_baseline. We keep comparability. But need to ensure preserved set covers the heavy hitters (low-latency, security prompts). We'll weight selection.

Ellie: Ops note: preserved baseline items must be immutable and stored with metadata: `source`, `added_by`, `variant_tags`, `sha256`. Add a `lock` flag to prevent accidental rotation.

Ravi: For metrics: use two-tier signals. Immediate (canary): pass/fail thresholds on generation time and semantic delta (embedding cosine < 0.92). Long-term: distributional drift (KL on token probs), generation entropy delta, and answer stability (Jaccard on normalized answers).

Maria: What thresholds? We should avoid being too strict and generating noise. Maybe canary embedding cosine < 0.92 or latency > +40% => fail. Long-term KL > 0.06 over 14d => flag.

Sanjay: For stochasticity run n=3 samples on canary with different seeds and compute median metric. Also track variance; high variance => mark as flaky and require extra runs.

Ellie: Human flow: any canary fail should open `triage` with `needs-investigation`. Auto-hold rollout and notify owners. For long-term flags, create a `monitoring` ticket and schedule a deeper pass.

Kai: Implementation sketch in config terms:```
bench_pools:
  preserved_baseline:
    pct: 0.07
    frozen_days: 90
  rolling_pool:
    pct_weekly: 0.15
    stratify_by: [domain, seqlen, lang]
  canary_pool:
    size: 20
signals:
  canary:
    embedding_cosine_threshold: 0.92
    latency_increase_pct: 40
    samples: 3
  long_term:
    kl_threshold: 0.06
    window_days: 14
    entropy_delta: 0.15
```

Ravi: Suggest storing per-sample provenance: `previous_model_outputs` (hashes) to detect hallucination drift. Also track `token_budget_used` per pool so we can cap deepbench spend.

Maria: How do we handle model variants? We need per-variant preserved_baseline or at least per-arch/quant tag. Otherwise we confuse quantization-induced diffs with regressions.

Kai: We'll namespace gold indices by `model@version:variant` and maintain a mapping so preserved_baseline for `mymodel@v7` will point to separate preserved sets for `fp16` vs `int8`. For cross-variant comparisons, run a small delta bench.

Sanjay: Edge case: multi-lingual prompts with tokenization differences across tokenizers. We should detect tokenizer mismatch by comparing token counts and flag samples that change tokenization drastically. That can be excluded from auto-canary.

Ellie: Operational runbook snippet:
1) Canary runs on every prerelease build. If canary fails -> hold and notify.
2) Rolling pool updates occur weekly in dry-run first week. If dry-run shows >2 flags across rolling_pool, abort rotation.
3) Preserved baseline rotated only after a review (manual override).

bench-bot: bench-bot: scheduled dry-run for rolling_pool completed 1774701200: dry-run flagged 3/120 samples, variance high on 2 samples. Ticket #B-1480 created.

Kai: Good call. We should add a `dry_run_threshold` config: abort if flagged_pct > 1.5%.

Ravi: For cost control, cap `rolling_pool_tokens_per_week` and implement graceful degradation: when budget low, preferentially keep preserved+canary, drop extra rolling tests. Also have `dry_run_mode` so we don't consume tokens.

Maria: Who picks this up? I can own the preserved_baseline selection heuristics. Sanjay you own metric implementation. Ellie on ops wiring. Kai will add to RFC. Ravi will help with provenance and budget hooks.

Sanjay: I'll add sampling + tokenizer-change detector to the bench runner.

Ellie: I'll update the triage UI to show pool membership and preserved `lock` status.

Kai: Thanks. I'll start the RFC addendum and include the config sketch and runbook steps. Please add edge cases here (rare-token-heavy, long-document regression) if you see them.
